title: WPMS/1719/2013 of Smt Sushila @ Sheela Devi Vs Amit Kumar Agrawal AND ANOTHER

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 1719 of 2013
Smt. Sushila alias Sheela Devi Ö Petitioner
Vs
Shri Amit Kumar Agrawal & another Ö Respondents
Mr. Kanwaljit Singh, Advocate, present for the petitioner
Honíble B.S. Verma, J. (Oral)
 By means of this writ petition, the petitioner has
prayed for to issue a writ or direction in the nature of
certiorari for quashing the order dated 11.07.2013 passed by
learned Civil Judge (S.D.), Dehradun in Suit No. 257 of 2013,
Smt. Sushila @ Sheela Devi Vs Shri Amit Kumar Agrawal &
another whereby notices were issued to the
respondents/defendants on the application filed under Order
38 Rule 5 of C.P.C. by the petitioner to attach the property
before judgment.
 The ground mentioned in the application filed
under Order 38 Rule 5 of C.P.C. is that the land was acquired
by the State Government, under the provisions of Land
Acquisition Act, prior to the execution of the sale deed by the
defendants in favour of plaintiff/petitioner. The defendants,
by playing fraud executed the sale deed in favour of the
plaintiff and received the amount of `95,00,000/- (Rupees
Ninety Five Lakhs only). Therefore the suit for recovery of the
amount along with interest has been filed before the court
below.
 Mr. Kanwaljit Singh, counsel for the petitioner
further contended if the amount is withdrawn by the
defendants/respondents from the possession of the Land
Acquisition Officer, the purpose of the suit would be frustrated
as it will be difficult to recover the amount from the
defendants.

2
 From the perusal of the impugned order, it
transpires that the notices were issued to the defendants on
the application of the plaintiff and the trial court has fixed the
date 29.07.2013 for hearing on the application filed under
Order 38 Rule 5 of C.P.C.
 Since the date is fixed 29.07.2013, in the facts and
circumstances of the case, learned trial court is directed to
hear the application filed under Order 38 Rule 5 of C.P.C. by
the plaintiff/petitioner as early as possible, preferably within
eight weeks from the date of production of the certified copy of
this order. It is further directed that unnecessary
adjournments be avoided and the parties are also directed to
cooperate in the expeditious disposal of the application filed by
the plaintiff/petitioner under Order 38 Rule 5 of C.P.C.
 In case, the defendants/respondents have not been
served for some reason till 29.07.2013, the petitioner is given
liberty to take steps for service upon the
defendants/respondents by Dasti notices. Learned Civil
Judge (S.D.), Dehradun is directed that in case, such
application, for Dasti notices, is moved by the
petitioner/plaintiff, he may be permitted to serve them by
Dasti notices. Thereafter, the learned trial court shall decide
the application under Order 38 Rule 5 of C.P.C. on merit
within the period mentioned above.
 With the aforesaid observation, the writ petition is
disposed of.
